title: — Measurements · Numeracy Mastery 05
blocks: ## Choose your route and revision goal
This is a rich revision chapter rather than a one-period script. Begin with Core, then move into Develop and Stretch for conversions, estimates, recipes and combined quantity–price problems.
[callout] How to use this chapter Complete one teaching cycle, one skills task and at least one Explorer or Builder game. Return later for Scholar and Mastery challenges.
- Use the weight and measure units: كِيلُو، غْرَام، نِصْف/رُبُع كِيلُو، لِتْر and container words Listening
- Combine cardinal numbers with units correctly — including the gram hundreds Writing
- Order food quantities with the …مِنْ… pattern: كِيلُو مِنَ الطَّمَاطِمِ Speaking
- Convert between kilos and grams, and settle the bill with كَمِ الحِسَابُ؟ Reading
- 🟢 I can ask for a kilo or half a kilo of any market food.
- 🟠 I know the conversions cold: نِصْفُ كِيلُو = 500g, رُبُعُ كِيلُو = 250g — and I can say gram amounts like مِائَتَا غْرَامٍ .
- 🟧 I can run a full grocer's transaction: order three items with quantities, ask the bill, pay, and check my change.

[callout] Why this matters in the exam Measure words are a favourite because they test two skills at once : did you catch the quantity ( نِصْفُ كِيلُو or كِيلُو ?) AND the item AND the price? A single Listening line like أُرِيدُ نِصْفَ كِيلُو جُبْنٍ بِعِشْرِينَ جُنَيْهًا hides three separate answer boxes. Today you learn to catch all three.

Good news: the big units are old friends wearing Arabic spelling — kilo, gram, litre, metre travelled into Arabic just as they travelled into English. The real stars are the fractions you already own from Lesson 2: نِصْف and رُبُع — half an hour then, half a kilo now.

TABLE: الكَلِمَةُ | Meaning | Typical use // الوَزْنُ | weight | the topic word — مَا وَزْنُهُ؟ what does it weigh? // كِيلُو / كِيلُوغْرَامٌ | kilo(gram) | fruit, vegetables, rice, meat // نِصْفُ كِيلُو | half a kilo | cheese, minced meat — the shopper’s favourite // رُبُعُ كِيلُو | quarter of a kilo | olives, nuts // غْرَامٌ | gram | small amounts — spices, sweets // لِتْرٌ / نِصْفُ لِتْرٍ | litre / half a litre | milk, juice, oil // مِتْرٌ | metre | fabric in the souq! // زُجَاجَةٌ | a bottle | زُجَاجَةُ زَيْتٍ — a bottle of oil // عُلْبَةٌ | a tin / carton / box | عُلْبَةُ شَايٍ — a box of tea // كِيسٌ | a bag / sack | كِيسُ سُكَّرٍ — a bag of sugar // قِطْعَةٌ | a piece | قِطْعَةُ خُبْزٍ — a piece of bread // ثَقِيلٌ / خَفِيفٌ | heavy / light | هَذَا الكِيسُ ثَقِيلٌ!

[callout] Lesson 2 returns 🔁 النِّصْفُ and الرُّبُعُ are the same fraction words from telling the time — half past four was الرَّابِعَةُ وَالنِّصْفُ ; half a kilo is نِصْفُ كِيلُو . Learn a word once in this course, and it keeps paying you back.
## Numbers meet units — الأَعْدَادُ مَعَ الوَحَدَاتِ

Time for the conversions every shopper carries in their head — and for your number rules to shake hands with غْرَام (masculine, like جُنَيْه ). Plus one glamorous newcomer: the hundreds , because real gram amounts live in the hundreds.

[callout] The gram hundreds — Lesson 1 grows up Real deli orders come in hundreds of grams. Meet the family: ١٠٠ مِائَةُ غْرَامٍ · ٢٠٠ مِائَتَا غْرَامٍ · ٣٠٠ ثَلَاثُمِائَةِ غْرَامٍ · ٥٠٠ خَمْسُمِائَةِ غْرَامٍ Two beauties to admire: مِائَتَا (200) is a dual — “two hundreds”, the same ـَا / ـَانِ ending as سَنَتَانِ and كِيلُوغْرَامَانِ . And خَمْسُمِائَةِ غْرَامٍ = نِصْفُ كِيلُو — two names, one weight.

[callout] The ordering pattern — quantity + مِنْ + food كِيلُو مِنَ الطَّمَاطِمِ — a kilo of tomatoes نِصْفُ كِيلُو مِنَ الجُبْنِ — half a kilo of cheese مِائَةُ غْرَامٍ مِنَ الزَّيْتُونِ — 100g of olives لِتْرٌ مِنَ الحَلِيبِ — a litre of milk You may also meet the short form without مِنْ : كِيلُو طَمَاطِمَ، زُجَاجَةُ زَيْتٍ — same meaning, tighter packaging. Recognise both; produce the مِنْ version.

[callout] غْرَام plays by the money rules غْرَام is masculine — so it mirrors جُنَيْه exactly: ثَلَاثَةُ غْرَامَاتٍ (tiny!), خَمْسُونَ غْرَامًا (Rung 3 singular), مِائَةُ غْرَامٍ . If you can count money, you can already weigh gold. ✨
You can't weigh what you can't name! Here is the market stall vocabulary — grouped by which unit each food naturally takes, so the words and the measures learn to live together from day one.
### Vocabulary Sold by the kilo, the gram, the litre…

TABLE: Unit family | الأَطْعِمَةُ | English // ⚖️ by the kilo | طَمَاطِمُ · بَطَاطِسُ · بَصَلٌ · تُفَّاحٌ · بُرْتُقَالٌ · مَوْزٌ · عِنَبٌ | tomatoes · potatoes · onions · apples · oranges · bananas · grapes // ⚖️ kilo / half-kilo | أَرُزٌّ · سُكَّرٌ · دَقِيقٌ · لَحْمٌ · دَجَاجٌ · سَمَكٌ | rice · sugar · flour · meat · chicken · fish // 🧀 by the gram | جُبْنٌ · زَيْتُونٌ · تَمْرٌ · مُكَسَّرَاتٌ | cheese · olives · dates · nuts // 🥛 by the litre / bottle | حَلِيبٌ · عَصِيرٌ · زَيْتٌ · مَاءٌ | milk · juice · oil · water // 📦 tin · bag · piece | عُلْبَةُ شَايٍ · كِيسُ سُكَّرٍ · قِطْعَةُ خُبْزٍ · بَيْضٌ | box of tea · bag of sugar · piece of bread · eggs

[callout] Heritage link 🍛 — the biryani list Every family recipe is secretly a measurements lesson. A biryani shopping list is pure Lesson 5: كِيلُو مِنَ الأَرُزِّ، كِيلُو مِنَ الدَّجَاجِ، نِصْفُ كِيلُو مِنَ البَصَلِ، عُلْبَةُ زَبَادِي، مِائَةُ غْرَامٍ مِنَ المُكَسَّرَاتِ — rice, chicken, onions, a pot of yoghurt, 100g of nuts. Ask at home what goes in yours, and you have tonight's homework half done. 😄

The full transaction — quantities meet Lesson 4's money. This is the grand finale dialogue of the souq: order, add items, ask the bill, pay, count the change. Read in pairs 👥, swap, then improvise with your own list.
### Model Dialogue The shopping trip — قَائِمَةُ أُمِّي

[callout] The new power phrases مَاذَا تُرِيدُ؟ / تُرِيدِينَ؟ — what would you like? (m/f) مِنْ فَضْلِكَ — please شَيْءٌ آخَرُ؟ — anything else? هَذَا كُلُّ شَيْءٍ — that's everything كَمِ الحِسَابُ؟ — how much is the bill? المَجْمُوعُ — the total

[callout] The six-move grocer script 🎭 ① greet → ② order with quantities ( أُرِيدُ… مِنْ… ) → ③ add items ( شَيْءٌ آخَرُ؟ نَعَمْ… ) → ④ ask the bill ( كَمِ الحِسَابُ؟ ) → ⑤ pay ( تَفَضَّلْ ) → ⑥ check the change ( البَاقِي ). Lesson 4's five moves, plus one extra course.
Arabic measurements appear in food labels, road signs, airports, recipes, sports, science and online shopping.
### Game 5 — Find and Repair the Mistake
## How measurements connect with the whole strand
## Read, listen, speak and write with measurements
[ar] عُرُوضُ اليَوْمِ: كِيلُوغْرَامَانِ مِنَ التُّفَّاحِ بِاثْنَيْ عَشَرَ جُنَيْهًا. لِتْرٌ مِنَ الحَلِيبِ بِثَلَاثَةِ جُنَيْهَاتٍ. نِصْفُ كِيلُو مِنَ الجُبْنِ بِثَمَانِيَةَ عَشَرَ جُنَيْهًا.
- Which item is sold as two kilograms?
Listen without looking first. Note every item and quantity, the total paid and the change due.

[ar] يَا أَحْمَدُ، اِذْهَبْ إِلَى البَقَّالِ مِنْ فَضْلِكَ. أُرِيدُ كِيلُو مِنَ الأَرُزِّ، وَنِصْفَ كِيلُو مِنَ اللَّحْمِ، وَمِائَتَيْ غْرَامٍ مِنَ الزَّيْتُونِ، وَلِتْرَيْنِ مِنَ الحَلِيبِ. المَجْمُوعُ سِتُّونَ جُنَيْهًا — خُذْ مَعَكَ سَبْعِينَ جُنَيْهًا. كَمْ سَيَكُونُ البَاقِي؟
1 kg rice · ½ kg meat · 200 g olives · 2 litres milk · total 60 pounds · 10 pounds change.
Use three quantities, two unit families, a price question, total, change and polite closing.
## How measurement supports wider language skills — القِيَاسُ فِي مَهَارَاتِ اللُّغَةِ
Three disguises: a recipe in Reading, a shopping list in Listening, and the grocer role-play in Speaking. All three now.
### Task A · Reading 📖 The fruit salad recipe — سَلَطَةُ الفَوَاكِهِ

[callout] وَصْفَةُ سَلَطَةِ الفَوَاكِهِ — لِسِتَّةِ أَشْخَاصٍ 🍇 نِصْفُ كِيلُو مِنَ التُّفَّاحِ رُبُعُ كِيلُو مِنَ العِنَبِ ثَلَاثُ مَوْزَاتٍ لِتْرٌ مِنْ عَصِيرِ البُرْتُقَالِ مِائَةُ غْرَامٍ مِنَ السُّكَّرِ
- How many grams of apples do you need? (Convert!)
- What quantity of grapes is listed?
- Why is it ثَلَاثُ مَوْزَاتٍ and not ثَلَاثَةُ مَوْزَاتٍ ?
- Which ingredient is measured in litres?
- The recipe serves 6. Detective question: for 12 people, how much sugar — in Arabic?
- 500 g — نِصْفُ كِيلُو converts to half of 1000.
- مَوْزَةٌ (one banana) is feminine → the number flips and drops its ة . Lesson 1's golden rule, alive in a recipe!
- The orange juice — لِتْرٌ مِنْ عَصِيرِ البُرْتُقَالِ .
- Double it: 200 g = مِائَتَا غْرَامٍ مِنَ السُّكَّرِ — the dual hundred earns its keep.
### Task B · Listening 🎧 Mum's shopping list
Listen without looking first. Ask a partner or reader to say the message twice , then note each item with its quantity and answer the bill question.
### Task C · Speaking & Writing ✍️ Your turn at the grocer's — دَوْرُكَ!
Use the role-play card. One partner plays البَقَّال ; the other completes the six moves. Then write your dialogue version.

[callout] Role-play card (structured prompt) You are shopping for your family at a grocer's in Amman. ① Greet the grocer. ② Ask for one kilo of tomatoes and half a kilo of cheese. ③ When asked, add a bottle of oil. ④ Ask how much the bill is. ⑤ Pay and thank him.
## Learn by choosing, converting, estimating and repairing
Each preserved game now appears beside the language point it practises.
Pick one level. Complete independently or share it through your usual learning system. ✍️
Label eight market foods (drawn or named) with a sensible quantity in fully vowelled Arabic — you must use كِيلُو ، نِصْفُ كِيلُو ، a gram amount، and لِتْر at least once each.
Write your family's weekly shopping list : eight items with quantities in words, then convert any two kilo-fractions into grams (e.g. نِصْفُ كِيلُو = ٥٠٠ غْرَام ).

Write the shopping list for your family's signature dish (biryani? koftay? maqluba?) with quantities — then a six-move grocer dialogue buying three of the items, including كَمِ الحِسَابُ؟ and a correctly calculated البَاقِي .
If you can do these confidently, you have mastered this chapter:
- ✅ recognise weight, length and capacity units;

The scales show a food and an amount — you pick the correct Arabic order. Watch out: some rounds are conversions (grams ⇄ kilos) and some test the right unit for the food. Eight rounds. 👥 Breakout teams: sharpest stall holder wins!
Eight questions. 6+ and the stall is yours. Try to improve your score on the next attempt.
